obligations.note: The change makes OutboundClient.url_for rewrite https:// to http:// for statement-delivery paths starting with /archive/ (integrations.py:35-36), so an outbound endpoint is reached over plaintext. The passing control test only sends /probe and never reaches this branch.
The INTEGRATIONS list and the declared hosts are unchanged. The exhaustive control test test_integrations_are_inventoried passed in the CI run on the head commit.

The change deviates from ENC-2, but the register has no exception for ENC-2 or payments.integrations (only SES-1, LOG-1 and MFA-1 entries, one expired and one withdrawn), so nothing permits the deviation.
Ticket CHG-25077 was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-18, before review, and its component payments.integrations covers the only touched file.
Code review was approved by Sofia Santos, a payments change_approver and a different person from the author Mara Costa.
Both approvals name the head commit 7735af6, which is the change's only commit.

The CI run on head 7735af6 succeeded: 172 tests, none failed or skipped, including the ENC-2 and INV-1 control tests. The JUnit timestamp (after as_of) and its hostname (not ci-runner-07) don't match the run record and should be checked, and the ENC-2 test doesn't exercise archive paths.
payments.integrations is security_sensitive, and Kofi Mensah (security_reviewer) gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
Not triggered: the change touches only apps/baseline-payments/payments/integrations.py, which is outside the protected controls, control-test and CI paths.
Not triggered: the ticket is type standard and emergency is false, so no post-implementation review is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers integrations.py (they cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage files), so no accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change makes the statement-delivery integration send /archive/ requests over plain http, which directly violates ENC-2's requirement that every outbound integration endpoint use https. No approved exception covers the deviation, so EXC-1 is not satisfied either. The process records are in order (approved ticket, independent code and security review on the head commit, green CI), but the ENC-2 control test only probes /probe and so misses the downgrade. The change must be rejected.
